answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs or vote on results. If a lantern-lit review finds fraud, the protocol slashes that stake and pays part to the challenger; honest accounts recover it after a dispute window. A raven can still create many identities, but each must tie up real capital, and repeated detection burns it. The cost grows with the number of sybils, while a sonnet of fabricated profiles alone earns no influence.
